topic: BLK-20260901-gen2-40-to-123 residual: native binary write rc=19 at merged_ir_functions=13107

root_cause.rc19: NativeCompiler.code_overflow -- NC_BIG_CODE (native ELF code buffer) fixed at 8 MiB (nc_code_capacity_bytes()); self-hosted/compiler/main.sio's own generated machine code exceeded it.
root_cause.rc20: NativeCompiler.reloc_overflow -- NC_FLAT_RELOC_* (flat relocation table, 4 parallel arrays) fixed at 131,072 entries (nc_flat_reloc_capacity()); the same self-compile exceeded it once rc19 was cleared and the compile advanced.

method: Added true unconditional counters (code_overflow_bytes_attempted, reloc_overflow_count_attempted) to NativeCompiler so each overflow branch reports the exact size needed, not an estimate. Measured via scripts/dev/souc-build-remote.sh --gate gen2-progress on gpuorangefs-r770-proxmox (32 CPUs), then sized each capacity bump with real headroom against the measured number. scripts/ci/native_capacity_tiers_gate.sh / native_capacity_tiers_check.py (the static declaration/accessor coherence tripwire) updated in the same commit; its rc19/rc20 regexes were loosened to allow a diagnostic body, matching the existing rc22/label_overflow precedent.

capacity_changes.note: Sized to hold NC_BIG_CODE(128 MiB) + rodata(256 KiB) + data(256 KiB) + page-alignment padding with margin. Not independently overflow-measured; no rc fired against it in any run below.

gate_ratchet.reason: Gate is a ratchet: red on falling short OR going further than the recorded rung. Reaching gen2 (below) is real, reproduced progress and must be banked per the gate's own fail message, else the next run would go red for the wrong reason.

residual.description: gen2.elf is a valid ELF, compiles rc=0, but `gen2 --version` does not print output souc_banner recognizes as either 'madaros' or 'lean_single' (scripts/lib/souc_invoke.sh). madaros_fixed_point_gate.sh: 'the payload is wrong, not merely different'. Reproduced identically across two independent runs (same gen1_elf_sha256).
residual.scope_note: Not touched by this fix. This is a distinct, undiagnosed class of issue (gen2 runtime/self-identification behavior) separate from the native-writer capacity walls this receipt covers. Root cause not yet investigated: could be anywhere from a --version dispatch bug to a deeper miscompile in gen2's own emitted code.
residual.next_step: Needs its own diagnosis pass: capture gen2's actual --version stdout/stderr (not just the banner classification), and check whether gen2 crashes, hangs, or prints something unexpected.
